title: Forward Deployed Software Engineer
description:
About TruKKer and the Role TruKKer is hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer who owns the full journey from a business problem to a solution people actually use, building with Claude Code on top of our existing systems. TruKKer is a technology-driven road freight and logistics company. Our business teams run on fast-moving, process-heavy workflows, and many of their pain points are best solved by small, well-targeted software rather than long project cycles. The Forward Deployed Engineer sits inside that gap: one person, embedded with the business, who can understand a problem, decide what to build, build it, prove it works, roll it out and keep it useful. There are no hand-offs between a business analyst, a product manager, a developer and a tester. The Forward Deployed Engineer is all of them for the solutions they own. 
 If you prefer working from requirements someone else has already written, this is not the role. If you would rather spend a morning with an operations team, find where hours are leaking every week, and have something working in front of them soon after, read on. 
 Role Summary The Forward Deployed Engineer is the single owner of a solutions entire lifecycle. You start by understanding what the business team is struggling with, and you finish only when the team is using the solution and getting value from it. 
 In practice you will: Spend time with business teams to find and define real problems, not just take requests. Research the product options and gather requirements from the right stakeholders. Build the solution end to end using Claude Code, either as an enhancement to an existing system or a new build from scratch. Test it yourself, end to end, before anyone else sees it. Train the business team, launch the solution and stay on as its owner. Track adoption, and when usage is low, find out why and fix it. 
 Key Responsibilities The work runs in seven stages. You own every one of them. 1. Discover and understand business challenges Work closely with business teams to learn how they operate day to day and where time, money or accuracy is being lost. Identify and prioritise the problems worth solving, using impact, effort and urgency. Define each problem clearly, with a measurable outcome, before any solution is proposed. 2. Research and define the solution Research the product space: how similar problems are solved elsewhere, and whether to enhance an existing system or build something new. Gather and document requirements from the relevant stakeholders (business users, managers, data owners, engineering). Propose a solution with scope, trade-offs and success criteria, and get alignment before building. 3. Build end to end with Claude Code Design and develop the solution using Claude Code, either as an enhancement within TruKKer’s existing systems or as a new build from scratch. Handle the full stack of the solution: data, logic, integrations, interface and deployment. Make sound decisions on architecture, security, access control and maintainability, and review AI-generated code with care. Keep documentation current so others can understand and support what you have built. 4. Test it yourself Own end-to-end testing: functional, integration, edge cases, data accuracy and user-flow checks. Validate with realistic business data and scenarios, and fix issues before release. 5. Train and implement Set up and run training and walkthrough sessions with the business team. Prepare simple guides or demos so users can adopt the solution without hand-holding. Manage the rollout and go-live, including the first weeks of hypercare. 6. Support and enhance Be the point of contact for business queries, issues and enhancement requests on your solutions. Triage and resolve issues quickly, and scope, build and ship enhancements as needs evolve. 7. Drive adoption Monitor whether each solution is actually being used, by whom and how often. If usage is low, sit down with the business to find the real reason (workflow fit, trust, training, missing features, process change). Provide and deliver the fix, whether that is a product change, more training or a process adjustment, until the solution is part of how the team works. 
 Required Skills and Qualifications We care more about what you can build and own than about the title on your last job. 3 to 6 years of experience in software engineering, solutions engineering, product engineering or a similar hands-on role. Strong full-stack ability: you can read and write backend logic, work with databases and APIs, and build a usable front end. Hands-on experience building with AI coding tools, ideally Claude Code, and the judgement to review, test and correct AI-generated code. Proven ability to take a vague business problem, break it down, and turn it into clear requirements and a working solution. Comfortable working inside existing systems: reading unfamiliar code, integrating with current tools and making safe changes. Disciplined self-testing habits, covering functional checks, edge cases and data validation. Excellent communication: you can talk to a non-technical operations team and a senior engineer in the same day, and run a good training session. High ownership and follow-through, with a bias for action and for finishing what you start. Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. 
 Nice to Have Experience in logistics, supply chain, freight, marketplaces or other operations-heavy businesses. Familiarity with ERP, TMS, CRM or similar enterprise systems and their integrations. Experience with BI and analytics tools for building dashboards and usage tracking. Prior experience in a forward deployed, solutions engineering or internal tools role. Product management exposure, such as writing PRDs, prioritising backlogs and running user research. Who You Will Work With You will work daily with business teams such as operations, sales, customer success and finance, and with the product, engineering and data colleagues who own the systems you build on. The business reaches out to you directly, so you must be comfortable being the face of the solution. 
 How Success Is Measured The Forward Deployed Engineer is judged on outcomes the business can feel, not on lines of code shipped. Targets are set with the hiring manager once the role is filled. Problem-solution fit — Solutions shipped that address a validated business problem, with a stated outcome Delivery speed — Time from problem identified to solution live Quality — Defects found after go-live, and rework needed after release Adoption — Share of intended users actively using the solution, and how that trends after launch Business impact — Time saved, errors reduced, or revenue or cost effect, versus the baseline Responsiveness — Time to respond to and resolve business queries and enhancement requests Stakeholder satisfaction — Feedback from business teams on trust, clarity and support

Key Skills: Product Engineering,Solution Engineering,Architecture,Deployment And Release Management,Full Stack,Code Review,Business Analysis,Backend

Discover and understand business challenges Work closely with business teams to learn how they operate day to day and where time, money or accuracy is being lost. Identify and prioritise the problems worth solving, using impact, effort and urgency. Define each problem clearly, with a measurable outcome, before any solution is proposed. 2. Gather and document requirements from the relevant stakeholders (business users, managers, data owners, engineering). Build end to end with Claude Code Design and develop the solution using Claude Code, either as an enhancement within TruKKer’s existing systems or as a new build from scratch. Handle the full stack of the solution: data, logic, integrations, interface and deployment. Test it yourself Own end-to-end testing: functional, integration, edge cases, data accuracy and user-flow checks. Validate with realistic business data and scenarios, and fix issues before release. 5. Train and implement Set up and run training and walkthrough sessions with the business team. Prepare simple guides or demos so users can adopt the solution without hand-holding. Manage the rollout and go-live, including the first weeks of hypercare. 6. Support and enhance Be the point of contact for business queries, issues and enhancement requests on your solutions. Triage and resolve issues quickly, and scope, build and ship enhancements as needs evolve. 7. Drive adoption Monitor whether each solution is actually being used, by whom and how often. If usage is low, sit down with the business to find the real reason (workflow fit, trust, training, missing features, process change). title: Associate Product Designer
description:
Candescent is a forward-thinking technology company transforming how financial institutions deliver Intelligent Banking experiences. We unite digital banking, account opening, and branch solutions that power and connect digital banking, account opening, and branch solutions-creating seamless engagement across digital, remote, and in-person channels. Our Experience-Led, Intelligence-Driven approach combines human-centered design with data, automation, and cloud-based innovation. Built on an API-first architecture, our extensible ecosystem enables institutions to adapt quickly, integrate easily, and unlock new opportunities for growth-turning every customer interaction into a moment of clarity, confidence, and connection. 
 Business Function: Design (Payments team) Reports to: Siriki Vardhan Location: Bangalore, India (Hybrid) Type: Full-time 
 Role Purpose We are looking for a designer who can create accessible, inclusive experiences across native mobile and web platforms, with guidance from senior designers as they build proficiency in problem framing and craft. This role is well suited to someone who is eager to learn, handles day-to-day ambiguity with support, and is actively developing their thinking and craft through feedback and mentorship. Key Responsibilities End-to-End Product Design Support end-to-end UX design across defined workflows - from problem framing through final flows and prototypes - with guidance from senior designers. Work with structured requirements and, with support, help translate them into intuitive solutions. Ensure all designs align with WCAG accessibility standards. Design seamlessly for both mobile and web with responsive logic. Visual Interaction Craft Deliver pixel-perfect UI with strong hierarchy, spacing, grid systems, and visual detailing. Craft purposeful micro-interactions and micro-animations that improve clarity and delight. Maintain consistency with the design system while pushing visual quality forward. Prototyping Experimentation Build high-fidelity prototypes showcasing complex interactions and behaviors. Run quick validation cycles to refine decisions based on feedback. Collaboration Learn to balance business goals, user needs, and engineering constraints, with input from senior designers and PMs. Communicate concepts clearly to PMs, engineers, and stakeholders at the squad level. Translate complex ideas into simple, digestible visual representations. Actively seek and apply feedback from senior designers to sharpen craft and judgment. Qualifications Experience Required Bachelors/masters degree in design, HCI, Human Factors Engineering, Product Design, Communication Design, Behavioral Science, or related field. 3+ years of experience in UX/UI Design with strong visual and interaction work. Portfolio demonstrating strong visual craft and emerging systems-level thinking. Experience designing for both web and mobile platforms. Strong expertise in visual hierarchy, layout systems, and working with a design system. Strong understanding of accessibility principles and WCAG guidelines. Solid grounding in UX fundamentals, cognitive load reduction, and heuristics. Good communication and storytelling skills. Advanced Figma proficiency, including components, variants, auto-layout, variables, and Dev Mode / Code Connect. Experience designing for cross-platform environments (iOS, Android, Web). 
Preferred/Good to have Familiarity with AI-assisted design or development tools (e.g. AI-assisted Figma workflows, code-generation copilots, or similar) and interest in applying them to design system workflows. Experience creating micro-interactions / animations. Hands-on coding experience (a plus, not required).
